newsitem.title: UK: XFM awarded London FM radio licence.
newsitem.headline: XFM awarded London FM radio licence.

text.p: XFM Ltd has been awarded a licence to broadcast to London on the FM waveband, the UK's Radio Authority said on Thursday.
Twenty-five groups had applied to broadcast on the 104.9 FM frequency, the last FM slot available for independent local radio use on a London-wide basis.
The new station will have access to a potential audience of almost six million adults in the London area.
XFM plans to offer "alternative' rock music aimed mainly at a 15-34 year-old audience.
XFM's backers include Luxembourg broadcast group CLT while its managing director and co-founder Chris Parry is the manager of veteran British rock band The Cure.
Those who missed out on the licence include Capital Radio Plc, which was seeking to move its AM oldies station to an FM frequency.
Other applicants included European radio group NRJ SA and The Edge, a consortium which included Radio One DJ Chris Evans and had the support of financier George Soros.
The 104.9 FM licence was previously occupied by Melody FM which vacated it after reception problems in south-west London.
